200.q: I open when the sky closes in and fold away when it clears. When the wind flips me inside out, I've lost the fight. What am I?
I have two blades that are useless apart; I only cut when my legs cross. What am I?
I have bristles and visit your mouth twice a day, yet I never taste a thing. What am I?
I have many rungs but no bell, and I take you higher while standing perfectly still. What am I?
Feed me air and I grow; poke me and I go out with a bang. What am I?
I fly only when I'm tied down, dancing with the wind on the end of a string. What am I?
I bite paper and leave two tiny metal teeth behind to hold the pages together. What am I?
I hum all day and keep a bulb that only shines when you open my door. What am I?
I have four tines and a handle, and I spear your dinner on its way to your mouth. What am I?
I hug your waist and have a row of holes so I can loosen as you grow. What am I?
I have a tongue that swings but cannot taste, and I only speak when struck. What am I?
I have one round foot and two arms the gardener holds, and I haul dirt and stones. What am I?
I have a head and a claw but no body, and I drive nails home. What am I?
I have a skin but no body, and I only sing when beaten. What am I?
I have a long handle and stiff bristles, and I chase dust across the floor. What am I?
I have a mouth that swallows letters and a little flag that goes up when I've been fed. What am I?
I have a glass head and a glowing wire heart, and I wake at the flick of a switch. What am I?
I stand all day in a field with my arms stretched wide, and the birds never trust me. What am I?
When one end of me goes up, the other must come down; two children ride me at the park. What am I?
I wear spines instead of leaves and can wait months between drinks. What am I?
I am a house you carry on your back and raise before dark. What am I?
I have twelve pages and hundreds of numbers, and you throw me away every January. What am I?
I rise when you have a fever and fall when it freezes, though I have no legs. What am I?
I have a needle that never sews, and it always searches for the same direction. What am I?
I have two wheels and no engine, and I only stay upright while we're moving. What am I?
I have three eyes stacked one above another, and drivers obey whichever one is open. What am I?
I make the brightest day look dim and hide your eyes from the crowd. What am I?
I fold in half, live in your pocket, and hold your cards and cash. What am I?
I start as a hard little kernel and burst into a fluffy white puff when heated. What am I?
Children build me with a bucket and a spade, and the tide takes me back every evening. What am I?
I have a head but no brain, and I get pounded into wood to do my job. What am I?
I have six strings and a hollow body, and I sing when strummed. What am I?
I sleep for centuries, then wake and spit fire from my top. What am I?
I am born in winter with a carrot for a nose, and I disappear when spring comes. What am I?
I catch the wind so a boat can move, though I have no engine at all. What am I?
I hold your place while you're away, tucked between the pages. What am I?
I take away mistakes and grow smaller with every one I fix. What am I?
I stand over water with my feet on both banks, and cars drive across my back. What am I?
I stand alone on the rocks and blink all night so ships keep their distance. What am I?

400.q: I have threads but no cloth, and a head that turns with a twist. What am I?
I take a hot bath, bleed my color into the water, and then get thrown away. What am I?
I lose my head the first time I'm used, and I'm useless after that. What am I?
I have six faces but wear no expression, and twenty-one dots but cannot see. What am I?
I am a single bent wire that holds pages together without leaving a hole. What am I?
I tell the truth every morning, and people step on me anyway. What am I?
I am a row of black stripes hiding a number, and I beep at the checkout. What am I?
I run through eyelets, get tied twice a day, and trip you when I'm loose. What am I?
No two of me are alike, and I'm left on everything you touch. What am I?
I only tell time when the sky is clear, with one hand that never moves. What am I?
I have a hole for a key but no key of my own, and I open for only one. What am I?
I have four strings and a bow but shoot no arrows, and I'm tucked under the chin. What am I?
I am a throat on the roof that swallows only smoke. What am I?
Bury me and I rise; I am the smallest thing a forest needs. What am I?
I am beaten with a stick at parties, and everyone cheers when I burst. What am I?
Tie me and I hold; pull me the wrong way and I only tighten. What am I?
I carry your face across borders and collect stamps from strangers. What am I?
I show only a tenth of myself, and the rest of me sank a famous ship. What am I?
I take your money without a word and drop your snack from behind glass. What am I?
I am a creature turned to stone, sleeping in rock for millions of years. What am I?
I grow inside a living shell, born from a grain of sand, and end up on a necklace. What am I?
I twist and pull, and without me the wine stays trapped. What am I?
Tip me over and all my brothers fall in a line; I wear spots on my face. What am I?
My arms turn all day without lifting a thing, and I grind grain when the breeze blows. What am I?
I open only when you're falling, and the air is what fills me. What am I?
I am art that bleeds while it's made, and I stay with you for life. What am I?
I tick like a clock but tell no time, and I keep musicians in step. What am I?
I drop and climb back up a string, and I can sleep at the bottom of it. What am I?
I come in twice a day and go out twice a day, pulled by something I never touch. What am I?
I am a river of ice that moves too slowly to see. What am I?
I flash before my loud brother arrives, and I can split a tree in a blink. What am I?
I am the mark a blow leaves behind; I bloom purple, then fade to yellow. What am I?
I am contagious but no disease; see me and you'll probably give me back. What am I?
I force your eyes shut for a split second, and strangers bless you for it. What am I?
I pull without hands and push my own kind away. What am I?
I am the slow orange fire that eats iron without a flame. What am I?
I am a yellow weed that turns into a white wish you blow away. What am I?
I am a sliver of wood small enough to hide under skin and make a grown man wince. What am I?
I hang around a doctor's neck and let a stranger hear your heart. What am I?
I show your bones without cutting you open. What am I?

600.q: I am easily made and easily broken; keeping me is the only hard part. What am I?
I travel fast, grow with every telling, and rarely arrive the way I left. What am I?
I am hard to make and harder to break, and I act before you decide. What am I?
The longer you keep me, the more of me there is, and I follow you until you pay. What am I?
I grow when you give me nothing and vanish when you give me something. What am I?
I'm easy to tell and hard to keep track of, and I need more of my kind to survive. What am I?
Alone I'm worth nothing, but stand me behind another number and I make it ten times bigger. What am I?
I am written by the winners and repeated by those who won't learn me. What am I?
I'm offered whenever I'm needed, and the more I'm used the less I'm believed. What am I?
I am held but have no handle, and carrying me hurts only the one who carries. What am I?
I am a virtue everyone needs but nobody wants to wait for. What am I?
I take years to build, seconds to break, and forever to repair. What am I?
The more attention you give me, the worse I get; ignore me and I fade. What am I?
I rise, curl, and crash on the shore, but I never bring the water with me; I'm just energy passing through. What am I?
I make the past look better than it ever was, and I ache sweetly. What am I?
I am the eerie feeling that you've lived this exact moment before, though you haven't. What am I?
I make your money worth less without taking a single note from your wallet. What am I?
I am cast but never caught, and counted but never spent. What am I?
I am a joke that earns a groan instead of a laugh, playing on two meanings at once. What am I?
I say the opposite of what I mean, and you know it only from my tone. What am I?
Shakespeare called me the green-eyed monster, and I grow when you compare yourself to others. What am I?
I happen thousands of times a day without your noticing, and I keep your eyes from drying out. What am I?
I promise to save you time, and I often cost you the most. What am I?
Everyone makes me, few admit me, and the wise learn from me. What am I?
I'm blamed when things go wrong and thanked when they go right, but I never planned any of it. What am I?
People work fastest just before I arrive, and I am often missed. What am I?
I am a line you can see but never reach; walk toward me and I walk away. What am I?
Read me backwards and I'm still the same; 'racecar' is one of me. What am I?
I am ruined the moment you hear about me. What am I?
I come at the very end, and without me the whole setup was for nothing. What am I?
Everyone has one of me; the wise keep me to themselves, and the loud can't. What am I?
I'm made on birthdays and shooting stars, and telling me is said to spoil me. What am I?
I arrive before you and stay after you leave, and one bad day can ruin me. What am I?
I am made entirely of people trying to get somewhere, and I go nowhere. What am I?
I tell strangers where you're from before you say it, and you can't hear your own. What am I?
I hang from a cave's ceiling and grow one drip at a time. What am I?
I am water shimmering in the desert that was never really there. What am I?
I am a hot spring that loses its temper on schedule, throwing water at the sky. What am I?
I raise the hair on your arms when you're cold or scared, and I'm named after a plucked bird. What am I?
